media.title: Store authoring: stable placement to publication
media.purpose: Provide a visibly labeled reviewed preview demonstrating that the real Store authoring HUD persists a default placement, reorders it, creates an immutable content version, and publishes through SQLite-backed services.
transcript: The Store scenario represents one million canonical pages covered by one template default and sparse selector sheets. The scale result is verified separately; this capture uses a disposable authoring database.
The authoring HUD crosses a validated server boundary into the same SQLite-backed services used by the domain proof.
A new stable placement key is added to the template default as an immutable block version.
Reordering writes an atomic order revision without changing the placement identity.
Editing creates another immutable version. The placement key remains stable while content provenance advances.
Publication compiles the current authoring revisions and atomically activates an immutable serving document.
The change survives in SQLite and serving reads the materialized pointer, not selector SQL.

captureState.scenarioScope: Store template default plus sparse chain, category, brand, and store-type selectors; the capture database is not the one-million-row benchmark database.
captureState.expectedInitialPublication: Assert an active foundation publication before recording; reset if publication would reuse an already matching authored input.

media.longDescription: The silent flow begins on the aggregated Store projection, opens live block authoring, adds weekend-promotion to the template default, reorders it, saves a new immutable version, publishes, and holds on the returned persisted publication state. The one-million-page claim comes from separate benchmark evidence, not this disposable capture database.

media.title: Eligible Vehicles: linked selector scope and copy on write
media.purpose: Provide a visibly labeled reviewed preview demonstrating that the real Eligible Vehicles HUD previews approved selector SQL, creates a linked sparse variant, performs a copy-on-write hero edit, and publishes deterministically.
transcript: Eligible Vehicles uses broader selector sheets. A page can match several layers, but distinct priorities make the result deterministic.
The persisted workspace resolves seven placements for the selected canonical page.
Selector SQL runs only during authoring preview or publication, against the approved surface.
A linked variant starts sparse: it inherits the default document and adds no copied page tree.
Editing inherited content is copy on write. Only the hero receives a local immutable version; the remaining placements stay inherited.
Publication validates priorities and conflicts before activating the materialized documents.
The result is a selector-scoped change with explicit provenance, not duplicated route content.

captureState.expectedInitialPublication: Assert the deterministic scenario publication and seven resolved placements before recording; fixture-only conflict cues must be labeled or excluded from live-success frames.

media.title: Structural replacement: stable key, tombstone, and rollback
media.purpose: Provide a visibly labeled reviewed preview demonstrating that the real Structural proof HUD preserves a placement key through a hero_alt edit, reverts and reapplies a tombstone, publishes atomically, and rolls back by pointer.
transcript: Structural replacement preserves the primary-hero placement key while the effective block type changes from hero to hero_alt.
This linked variant changes one hero, hides one promotion, and inherits twenty-two of twenty-four defaults.
A structural edit creates a new immutable hero_alt version without changing the document position.
Revert removes the local operation and restores inheritance. Hiding again writes an explicit scoped tombstone.
Publication atomically activates the conflict-free document and retains the previous immutable publication as a rollback target.
Rollback changes only the serving pointer. It does not recompile or mutate either publication.
Serving is restored to an existing immutable snapshot while authoring history remains intact.

captureState.scenarioScope: Structural page structural-page:hero-alt with primary-hero resolved as hero_alt, announcement-promo tombstoned, and 22 of 24 defaults inherited.
captureState.expectedInitialPublication: Assert an active structural publication and a retained predecessor before recording; rollback must remain guarded and must never be simulated.

media.alt: The Structural proof publication HUD after a stable-key hero_alt edit and scoped tombstone, with the immutable serving pointer restored to a retained predecessor.
media.longDescription: The silent flow begins with primary-hero retaining its placement key as hero_alt while 22 of 24 defaults remain inherited. It opens the linked variant, saves a new immutable hero_alt version, reverts and reapplies the announcement-promo tombstone, publishes a new snapshot, previews guarded rollback, confirms it, and holds on the restored immutable serving pointer.

media.title: Wall navigation: map search to persisted workspace
media.purpose: Demonstrate that the real production HUD narrows the Wall of Maps, opens the Store map and its persisted SQLite workbench, then returns through the same information architecture.
transcript: The Wall of Maps opens with the required scenario maps, their selector-sheet summaries, and the immutable-manifest serving posture.
Keyboard search narrows the inventory to the one Store map and keeps the bounded result count visible.
Inspect map opens the real persisted Store route and its sparse selector-sheet projection.
Block authoring reveals the live SQLite workspace: four visible placements, no tombstones, and one publication.
Primary navigation returns to the Wall with the Store filter retained for orientation.
Clearing search restores the complete three-map inventory without changing the information architecture.
The tutorial and operational workspace remain adjacent routes inside the same HUD shell.

media.title: Resolution pin: URL to layers, provenance, and serving seam
media.purpose: Demonstrate that one real Store projection point exposes its canonical URL, four ordered selector sheets, winning placement provenance, inspectible selector SQL, and independent route/content authority.
transcript: The Store projection exposes sparse selector sheets in explicit priority order.
The P30 McDonald's sheet and one concrete page point are selected; that page matches four sheets.
The resolution pin shows the canonical URL, tags, Camo route live, Auteur content published, and HTTP 200.
Matching sheets stay visible from the P0 template default through P10 chain, P20 fast food, and P30 McDonald's.
Expanding primary-hero shows the inherited version and the winning McDonald's replacement as complete provenance.
The exact approved selector SQL is inspectible, with an explicit warning that it runs only during preview or publication.
Returning to Trace restores the independent Camo Press and Auteur serving status for the selected point.
